chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Durust al-Wasiti, from Ijlan Abu Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman performing Tamattu' who arrived in Mecca and saw blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, then she sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf by the House; and if she does not become pure, when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water upon herself and begins with the Hajj from her house, and goes out to Mina and fulfills all the rituals.'

So when she arrives in Mecca, she performs two Tawafs by the House, then she performs Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. So when she does that, then everything is permissible for her except the bed of her husband.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills in Mecca)
key_terms.فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا: The bed of her husband (metonymy for sexual intercourse)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةٍ: A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj rituals for a menstruating woman performing Tamattu' who does not become pure before the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Hajj al-Tamattu' for menstruating women, emphasizing that the initial Tawaf al-Qudum and Sa'ee are performed in the state of major impurity (Junub/Hayd) without requiring Ghusl, a view supported by many Shia jurists. It further details the procedure for delaying the Tawaf al-Ifadah until the Day of Tarwiyah if menstruation persists, allowing the pilgrim to perform Ihram from her residence in Mecca. Upon completion, she attains full release from Ihram restrictions, with the sole exception of sexual intercourse with her husband.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Dorost Al Wasity, from Ijlan Abu Salih who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a woman performing Tumatto proceeding to Makkah, so she sees blood. Heasws said: ‘She would perform Tawaaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, then she would sit in her house. So if she becomes pure, she would perform Tawaaf by the House, and if she does not become pure, and it was the day of Tarwiyya (8th Zilhajj), she would pour water upon herself and begin with the Hajj from her house, and she would go out to Mina and fulfill the rituals, all of them.

So when she proceeds to Makkah, she would perform Tawaaf by the House with two Tawaafs. Then she would perform Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. So when she does that, then everything would be Permissible for her apart from the bed of her husband’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Durust al-Wasitiy from ‘Ajlan abu Salih who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who is for al-Hajj al- Tamattu‘ (advantageous). She enters Makkah and experiences Hayd (menses). He (the Imam) said, ‘She must perform Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah and remain at home. If she becomes clean, she must perform Tawaf around the House; but if she does not become clean on al-Tarwiyah (eight of Dhu al-Hajjah), she must pour water on herself and say Talbiyah for al-Hajj from her home, go to Mina’ and complete all the acts.

She then must come back to Makkah, perform two Tawaf then Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah. When she does this then she comes out of the state of Ihram and all things that were unlawful to her in the state of Ihram become lawful to her except the bed of her husband.’”
